latin.712: §. V. Succedit TERTIA Argumentorum CLASSIS, Rationativa quidem, sed sacra, i. e. mediò Revelationis terminô constans, quô infertur (1) ex Natura rei manducandæ spirituali, indignos nullô, eóque nec orali modo, corpus Christi manducare, quia nempe corpus Christi, cibus merè Spiritualis, est Supernaturalis, indeque modo merè Spirituali & Supernaturali sumendus.
latin.713: Sed Impii nihil Spiritualitatis supernaturalis possident, quô spiritualia capere possent. Præterea est cibus hujusmodi spiritualis, ut cum eo omnia bona spiritualia cohæreant, caro enim Christi assumta vivificat, & mundo manducanti dat vitam Joh. 6. tantóque magis, quanto idiomatum divinorum Communicatio abstracta id urget pressius.
latin.714: Quin, est spiritualis cibus, tantum Nutritivus, Augmentativus, Corroborativus, fidem alens & augens, non initium fidei conferens & impertiens: Hinc illis solis injunctus accipi, qui se ipsos probare possunt, num in fide sint? & post explorationem institutam, se in fide, imbecili licèt, deprehendunt esse, non aliis, qui vel se probare nequeunt ipsos, quales sunt Infantes, vel explorantes se, de Impietate ac impœnitentia sua per conscientiam convincuntur, quales sunt impii.
latin.715: Frustra excipitur AD PRIUS: Spiritualem cibum, etiam corporaliter oraliterque accipi posse, quando à Christo jubetur ita accipi, dicente: Edite, Hoc est Corpus meum. Resp. (a) de pane Christum loqui, quem per Hoc intelligit, teste Luthero pluribus in locis, utpote quem solum corporalibus manibus acceperat, fregerat & dederat, de eodem dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum. (b) Si item de Corpore suo locutus Christus est, & istud edere jussit, utique modum edendi haud alium intellexit, quàm à se, jam ante Cœnæ S. Institutionem, Joh. 6. edoctum, i. e. solum Spiritualem.
latin.716: Instas: Ita Mandatum Institutionis S. Cœnæ, Edite, duplicem obtinebit sensum, duos scil. edendi modos imperans, Corporalem scil. seu Oralem Panis benedicti, & Spiritualem corporis Christi. Respond. Concedendo totum, ceu non tantum non absurdum, sed penè necessarium, ob duplicem mandatô Christi oblatum cibum, Corporalem unum, alterum Spiritualem, ideoque ab iis ipsis, qui hanc instantiam formant, largiendum, quin tertio sensu ab iis ampliatum, quando primò, Oralem manducandi panis, secundo, Spiritualem manducandi corporis Christi, denique tertiò Sacramentalem seu Oralem manducandi itidem corporis Christi, Modum, mandatô Christi, Edite, comprehendi contendunt.
latin.717: Frustra item AD POSTERIUS excipitur: Homines omnes, naturâ suâ, Spiritu Sancto omnique spirituali vitâ cassos, nihilominus Spiritûs Sancti fieri participes idque mediante verbô, extrinsecè prædicato auditóque, mediante item aquæ baptismate, corpori administrato. Resp. (a) Non solam externam verbi divini prædicationem ac auditionem, nec solam aquæ baptismalis externam administrationem, sed internam Spiritus S. operationem adjunctam, corda humana regenerare & spiritualitate salvifica imbuere. (b) Cœnam S. non esse cum Verbo & Baptismate, ejusdem rationis, quandoquidem hæc Christiano vero ac genuino efficiendo, ista, jam tum effecto fideque donato inserviunt. Unde qui fide non instructus, uti corporis Christi, cibi merè spiritualis, non potest fieri particeps, ita per illud ipsum in fide corroborari & augeri nequit.
latin.718: (2) Ex natura Manducantium Impiorum, quia (a) sunt malitiosè repugnantes, Ergo Augmenti gratiæ divinæ prævenientis (quale augmentum in corpore Christi spiritualiter vivificante reponendum est) omnino ut incapaces, ita eodem indigni. Excipis, distinguendo inter Receptionem, & Retentionem carnis Christi; prius concedendum esse Impiis, non verò posterius. Respond. Rectius distingui hîc (ut aliàs Lutherani solent) inter Oblationem & Receptionem, quarum prior quidem competit in Impios per Gratiam Christi; posterior non item, ob malitiam eorum obstinatam, quæ ipsa quia Retentionem carnis Christi impedit sola, etiam pari ratione Receptionem ejusdem; Alias causa nulla esset, quare, obstante licèt Communicantis malitia, retineri tamen caro Christi non posset æquè, atque, obstante licet ejusdem malitia, recipi atque manducari.
latin.719: (b) Contra, Mandatum Christi, Cœnæ S. appropriant: Sunt enim inter non probantes semet, corpusque Christi non discernentes, quibus certè beneficium i. e. corpus Christi, in inobedientiæ suæ præmium, haud communicabitur. (c) Communione Sanctorum hominum tantisper exclusi, Ergo multò magis communione carnis Christi, non ad externam, cum Weigelianis & Swenckfeldianis, sed internam, cum Orthodoxis, Communionem, referenda, cujusque communione, omnibus & solis fidelibus competente, ceu communi quodam, spirituali tamen, vinculo glutineque, spiritualiter, tam cum Christo, quam inter se, uniuntur & uniti cohærent.

pass_a.712: §. V. There follows the THIRD CLASS of Arguments, Rational indeed, but sacred — i.e. consisting by a middle term of Revelation — by which it is inferred (1) from the spiritual Nature of the thing to be eaten, that the unworthy eat Christ’s body in no mode, and so neither orally, because namely Christ’s body, food merely Spiritual, is Supernatural, and therefore to be taken in a merely Spiritual and Supernatural mode.
pass_a.713: But the Impious possess nothing of supernatural Spirituality by which they could grasp spiritual things. Moreover food of this spiritual kind is such that with it all spiritual goods cohere — for Christ’s flesh assumed vivifies, and gives life to the world eating (Jn 6), and so much the more as the abstract Communication of divine idioms presses that more tightly.
pass_a.714: Nay, it is spiritual food only Nutritive, Augmentative, Corroborative, feeding and increasing faith, not conferring and imparting faith’s beginning: Hence it is enjoined to be received by those alone who can prove themselves, whether they are in faith — and after instituted examination find themselves to be in faith, though weak — not by others who either cannot prove themselves (as Infants) or examining themselves are convinced by conscience of their Impiety and impenitence (as the impious).
pass_a.715: In vain it is excepted TO THE FORMER: that Spiritual food can also be received corporally and orally when Christ commands it so received, saying: Eat, This is my Body. Reply (a) Christ speaks of the bread, which he understands by This, Luther witnessing in several places — inasmuch as that alone he had taken, broken, and given with corporal hands, saying of the same: This is my body. (b) If likewise Christ spoke of his Body and commanded it to be eaten, he certainly understood no other mode of eating than that taught by himself already before the Holy Supper’s Institution in John 6 — i.e. only the Spiritual.
pass_a.716: You press: Then the Mandate of the Holy Supper’s Institution, Eat, will obtain a double sense, commanding two modes of eating — Corporal or Oral of the blessed Bread, and Spiritual of Christ’s body. Reply: Conceding the whole, as not only not absurd but almost necessary, because of the double food offered in Christ’s mandate — one Corporal, the other Spiritual — and therefore to be granted by those themselves who form this instantia, nay amplified by them in a third sense when they contend that Christ’s mandate Eat comprehends first the Oral mode of eating bread, second the Spiritual of eating Christ’s body, and finally third the Sacramental or Oral mode of eating Christ’s body likewise.
pass_a.717: In vain likewise it is excepted TO THE LATTER: that all men, by nature void of the Holy Spirit and every spiritual life, nevertheless become partakers of the Holy Spirit through the word outwardly preached and heard, and through water baptism administered to the body. Reply (a) Not the external preaching and hearing of the divine word alone, nor the external administration of baptismal water alone, but the inward operation of the Holy Spirit joined thereto regenerates human hearts and imbues them with saving spirituality. (b) The Holy Supper is not of the same reason as Word and Baptism — inasmuch as these serve to make a true and genuine Christian, that serves one already made and gifted with faith. Whence he who is not furnished with faith cannot become partaker of Christ’s body, food merely spiritual, and so cannot be corroborated and increased in faith by that very thing.
pass_a.718: (2) From the nature of Impious Eaters, because (a) they are maliciously resisting — Therefore altogether as incapable of the Increase of preventing divine grace (which increase is to be placed in Christ’s spiritually vivifying body), so unworthy of the same. You except, distinguishing Reception and Retention of Christ’s flesh — the former to be granted to the Impious, not the latter. Reply: It is more rightly distinguished here (as Lutherans elsewhere are wont) between Oblation and Reception — of which the former indeed applies to the Impious through Christ’s Grace; the latter not likewise, because of their obstinate malice, which itself, since it alone impedes Retention of Christ’s flesh, also by like reason impedes Reception of the same; otherwise there would be no cause why, the Communicant’s malice obstructing, Christ’s flesh could nevertheless not be retained equally as, the same malice obstructing, it could be received and eaten.
pass_a.719: (b) Against this they appropriate Christ’s Mandate of the Holy Supper: For they are among those not proving themselves and not discerning Christ’s body, to whom certainly the benefit — i.e. Christ’s body — will not be communicated as reward of their disobedience. (c) Excluded for the time from the Communion of Saintly humans, Therefore much more from communion of Christ’s flesh — to be referred not to external communion with Weigelians and Schwenckfeldians, but to internal with the Orthodox — by which communion, belonging to all and only the faithful, as by a certain common yet spiritual bond and glue, they are united spiritually both with Christ and among themselves and cohere united.

712: §.V opens the third class: rational, but sacred — middle term from revelation.
(1) From the nature of the spiritual food: the unworthy eat Christ’s body in no mode, Oral included — it is merely spiritual and supernatural food, to be taken only that way.
713: The Impious have no supernatural spirituality by which to grasp spiritual things.
This food coheres with all spiritual goods: assumed flesh vivifies and gives life to the world that eats (Jn 6) — pressed harder still by communication of divine idioms.
714: Spiritual food only nourishes, augments, and corroborates faith — it does not plant faith’s start.

So it is commanded only for those who can prove they are in faith (even weak faith after self-examination) — not infants who cannot prove themselves, nor the Impious whose conscience convicts them of impenitence.
715: AD PRIUS is futile: “Eat, this is my body” does not prove spiritual food is taken corporally/orally.

Either Christ means the bread by “this” (Luther, many places — what hands took, broke, gave), or if he means his body, the eating-mode is the spiritual one he already taught in John 6 before the institution.
716: Press: then “Eat” has a double sense — oral of blessed bread and spiritual of Christ’s body.
Concede that — almost necessary given two foods in the mandate. Those who press the point even add a third: sacramental/oral eating of the body as well.
717: AD POSTERIUS is futile: Word and baptism making Spirit-participants does not prove Impious can take spiritual body-food.

Inward Spirit-operation regenerates, not bare hearing or water alone; and the Supper is not same-ratio with Word/Baptism — those make a Christian, this feeds one already gifted with faith. Without faith there is no partaking, and no increase of faith by that food.
718: (2a) From Impious eaters’ nature: they maliciously resist, so they are incapable of — and unworthy of — the increase of preventing grace placed in Christ’s vivifying body.

Do not split Reception vs Retention to give Impious reception. Better (as Lutherans elsewhere): Oblation reaches them by grace; Reception does not — the same obstinate malice that blocks retention blocks reception.
719: (2b) They stand against the Supper mandate — not proving themselves, not discerning the body — so Christ’s body is not given as prize for that disobedience.

(2c) Shut for now from the Saints’ human communion, they are shut much more from communion of Christ’s flesh — the Orthodox’s inward bond, not Weigelian/Schwenckfeldian externalism — uniting the faithful with Christ and each other. Stop §.V before §.VI.
